neighbours.label: the restricting word in a rule about what is permitted (may, only, except, other than)
fire: Visitors are permitted to photograph the exhibits only without flash.
No food is allowed in the library except bottled water.
Members may not use the pool other than during posted hours.
The software may be installed on one computer per license.
Students may bring only a pencil and an eraser into the hall.
Pets are not allowed in the building except for guide dogs.
You may copy these pages for personal, non-commercial use.
Parking is forbidden here other than for delivery vehicles.
quiet: Visitors often photograph the exhibits near the main entrance.
The library has a quiet room on the second floor with large windows.
Members enjoy the pool most during the summer afternoons.
The software was released last spring with a new interface.
Students sat in rows in the hall waiting for the exam to begin.
Many residents of the building own small dogs and cats.
These pages explain the history of the company in detail.
Delivery vehicles arrive here early each morning from the depot.

notes: Top examples come from terms of use and exam or club rules: 'may be used as part of', 'except for periods', 'other than as permitted', 'allowed to bring only'. Near misses: same rule-book or terms topics stated as plain facts with no restriction.
